summary: The article compiles IMF, S&P Global Market Intelligence, FICCI-IBA survey and SBI Caps views to argue India will remain one of the world's fastest growing economies over the next decade. It cites FDI inflows, a young population, a growing middle class and digitalisation as drivers, and forecasts GDP of $7.3 trillion by 2030. It also covers banking sector health, strong capex and global risks such as high US rates and geopolitical tension.
one_line: IMF, S&P and other analysts see India staying among the fastest-growing economies for a decade, driven by demographics, FDI, digitalisation and capex.
key_facts: The IMF said India is one of the large emerging economies doing better than expected and is a growth engine of the world economy.

S&P Global Market Intelligence forecasts India's nominal GDP in USD terms to rise from $3.5 trillion in 2022 to $7.3 trillion by 2030, exceeding Japan's GDP and making India the second largest economy in the Asia-Pacific region.
By 2022, India's GDP had already become larger than that of the UK and France, and by 2030 it is forecast to surpass Germany.
By 2030, 1.1 billion people in India will have internet access, more than doubling from an estimated 500 million internet users in 2020.
India's population surpassed China's earlier in 2023; China had been the most populous country for more than 300 years. India's median age is 28.2.
India is projected to account for 12.9 per cent of global growth over the next five years, surpassing the United States' 11.3 per cent share.
The Indian economy grew 7.2 per cent in the financial year ended March 2023 and 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of the current fiscal year.
The seventeenth FICCI-IBA survey covered January to June 2023 and included 24 banks representing about 79 per cent of the banking industry by asset size.

In the FICCI-IBA survey, 67 per cent of respondents indicated an increase in long-term infrastructure loans versus 57 per cent in the previous round, and 42 per cent of banks expect non-food industry credit growth above 12 per cent versus 36 per cent previously.
Gross NPA ratio of banks is at a decade low.
Indian real GDP growth is estimated at 6.2 per cent y/y in FY24 according to the SBI Caps note.
Union capital expenditure was up 48 per cent y/y in H1FY24, and major states' capex was up 45 per cent y/y in 5MFY24.
The fiscal deficit for 5MFY24 stood at 36% of the FY24BE, and gross direct tax revenue rose 18 per cent y/y up to October 9.
Rajan Jain of SBI Caps warned emerging markets with large USD-denominated debt are vulnerable to a strong DXY and high rates.
